utterances: F: Hi,um- I think my baggage was lost, and I need to I guess file a claim or I don't know what.
M: Okay, what flight were you on?
F: Um-Seventeen. Coming from --
M: On what airline?
F: It was Virgin Atlantic coming from London.
M: From London, okay. Um- And you went through all your proper checkpoints?
F: Yeah, I don't know where it was lost.  I was coming from Africa, so.
M: So you haven't seen your bags since Africa. You flew threw Heath Row to here.
F: Right.
F: Yeah.
M: Okay.  Well, let me see here. I-
M: It seems like it went through Heath Row.  I see it here. uh-
F: That's good.
M: But uh- I don't see it here in the airport yet. uh
M: I'm not sure where it is.  We can absolutely keep an eye out for for it for you.
F: Well, I can't leave without it. I mean, Could you find out?
M: Well, I'm not a miracle worker.  I don't know what I can do for you.  I don't have the bag right here.
F: Right, well can you get on the computer maybe and like track it down and see when it's going to get here?
M: Well, as I told you, it left Heath Row and it seems to have arrived here.  But if you can't find it, then-are you sure you know what your bag looks like?
F: Yes, sir, I know what my bag looks like.
M: Okay, and what is that?  What kind of bag is it?
F: Um- It's a travel backpack.  It's green and gray.  It's got my name on it and my information.
M: And you couldn't find it?
F: No, it didn't turn up at the baggage claim.
M: Are you sure?
F: I mean we've gone through all of this.  I've been to five people already who--
M: Well, obviously, that wasn't me, so I'm going to have to ask you the same questions they asked you just so we can get to the same point.
F: Okay.
M: All right?  Now, um- it's green, travel bag, you couldn't find it.  And was there something important in it that you need it?
F: Yes, lots of really like -- sentimental value only, but--
M: Sentimental value.
M: Right.  Well, I don't know what to tell you. Um- What I can offer you is a fifty dollar voucher on your next flight.
M: No, I understand. I mean. It's got to be tough all those sentimental things, but um- this is all I can do for you.
F: Does this happen often?  Do they--you just lose baggage and you just offer people money for it?
M: Well, you know, sometimes that's--really, I mean what else could we do?
F: Uh- Not lose the baggage in the first place. I mean You're offering a service here. I paid so much money for that ticket.
M: Well,
M: Obviously ma'am.
M: I am sorry, ma'am.
M: Let's- Let's just relax for a moment, ma'am.  You understand, obviously, we're going to do everything we can to keep all of your luggage here.
M: Obviously, we're not trying to lose your luggage.  Do you really believe that we're trying to lose your luggage ma'am?
F: No, but I mean like why can't- why can't you find it?  Where did it go?  Who lost it?
F: Well, I just-I paid so much money for this ticket.  I feel like you guys should be able to get-to offer me more than a fifty dollar voucher.
M: Well, we're talking about one bag.  You personally made it here, didn't you?

F: Yeah, meaning I didn't die in a fiery plane crash.  How convenient, but um- I paid two thousand dollar to ride your airline, and I would really appreciate getting my bags there to my destination in one place.
M: That's what the cost of the ticket was for.
M: Ma'am, international flights are not cheap and there's many reasons for that.  It does not have solely to do with your baggage or-
F: Right, but part of the agreement is that I'm paying so that I can take myself and my belongings with me.
M: Right. Yes, ma'am.
F: And that you're going to transport them safely from one place to another.
M: Right, and also if you'll read the fine print of your agreement you'll see that while we do bear some responsibility for lost luggage, it is a fifty dollar voucher.
F: That's all you can offer me? I mean, my the stuff in there is worth way more than fifty dollar.
M: Well, I understand that.  Did you buy flight insurance?
M: Well, my hands are really tied then.
F: Why do I need flight insurance?  Why don't you guys just guarantee that you're going to get the stuff that I leave with to my destination?
M: Well, it's like any kind of insurance.  You don't-when you get it, then you get more. You know, Like if you--
F: Right, but if I'm riding a bus, I don't need to buy luggage insurance that the backpack I take on is going to get to my destination with me.
M: Well, of course not because you've got your backpack with you the whole time.  Now, if you--you said this was a travel bag.  Why weren't you carrying it on if it was so important?
F: Because they made me check it.  It's too heavy.
M: Uh, so it was really heavy.
M: Well, you know what, it could still turn up, but until then I can offer you this fifty dollar voucher.
F: There's nothing else you can do?
M: I'm sorry, ma'am, there's nothing else I can do.  My hands are really tied here.  I really wish there was something else I could do for you.
F: I don't believe that for a second.
M: Well I don't know why you wouldn't believe that.
M: Obviously, I'm doing everything that I can here.
M: Well, I have no way to give you more money.  I'm giving you as much money as I can, and figuring- as far as figuring out where you bag is-
F: What do you mean as you can?  Who makes up these rules?
M: makes up?
F: You're an autono- autonomous human being.  You could- You could go into the com-
M: The airline makes these rules, mom ma'am.
F: So I'm just supposed to oh, well, oops, my luggage is gone and be fine with that and take your stinking fifty dollar voucher?
M: Well, you can take my stinking fifty dollar voucher and go home and wait and see if your luggage turns up. And if it does, then we'll deliver it to you.
F: And you have no guarantee.
M: I have no guarantee, absolutely not.
F: This is ridiculous.
M: How can I guarantee finding your luggage when it's lost?
F: Uh- Because you guys lost it, so it should be your responsibility to find it, too.
M: Right, well, when you're at home and you lose something, do you guarantee that you're going to find it later on?
F: Oh, come on.  Would you cut it out?  This is ridiculous.
M: Well, it sounds to me like you're being ridiculous
F: No, I don't think I am.  I like have a whole bunch of stuff that means a lot to me, and I brought it you know from Africa.  It's not like I can just go back and get it whenever I want.
M: Right.
F: It's not like I can go to Kmart and buy another.
M: I understand that, ma'am, but things get lost.  There's nothing I can do about that.  Things happen.  Accidents happen.
M: And while I really would love to be able to hand you your bag right now, obviously I can't do that.
M: So you'd like the fifty dollar voucher?
F: Yeah, I'll take your fifty dollar voucher.
M: Okay, just fill out these three forms, and um- you'll- we'll have that sent to you within the next three weeks and, of course, we'll definitely keep an eye out for your bag.
F: Thanks.
M: You have a wonderful day.
